pillar_reactions.evidence: Agreed without engaging on the merits and immediately redirected to the question he actually cared about: 'Oh, yeah, that's fine. I'm still just not understanding, like, the clear, like, packages. Like, if he works one-on-one, does it need to be every program?' Notably the pillar was mismatched to him and neither party dwelt on it — the rep acknowledged 'mobility is already on the good side for you', but the daily mobility protocol was still presented, when the prospect's disclosed problem is the opposite of stiffness: hypermobility with weak stabilisers.

Pushed back on the substance and on its inclusion at all. Before the pillar was delivered he had already said 'I wouldn't necessarily say that nutrition's on my highest, but if it's part of the program, sure', and after it he objected to the premise of the whole bundle: 'being that I'm not someone who is super lazy, I'm pretty aware of, like, movement and I work in the fields. I want something that is effective, that gets me what I need, but, like, being held by the hand for every single thing in my life, like, I don't think I'm that client, to be honest.'

Rejected pre-emptively in his very first answer, before any pillar was presented: 'I don't necessarily need someone texting me every day. I'm not interested, to be honest, but just being told like on technique check-ins, especially before I progress in weight, I would like to just be told about form.' He restated it twice more — 'the accountability doesn't scare me' and 'I don't think I'm that client'. The pillar the programme leans hardest on was the one this prospect actively did not want, and it was presented in full anyway.

anchors.raw: I've always noticed that when I did do like a little kettlebell work with like a personal trainer in the past, I always enjoyed it because of the movement and the, like, multilateral.
anchors.competitor: In-person personal trainer he previously worked with on kettlebells
anchors.note: No price was ever attached to this, so it is an expectation anchor rather than a numeric one — but it set the delivery model in his head before the call and it is what the offer was ultimately measured against. His reference for kettlebell coaching is a person in a room correcting him live, which is precisely the feature neither tier provides. He also noted that 'personal trainers in my area don't advertise specifically like focusing on kettlebell', which is why he was on the call at all: he wanted his existing model with kettlebell expertise added, not a different model.

unmet_demand.want: Periodic live, synchronous form correction — a private session weekly or fortnightly to check technique before progressing in weight
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Neither tier includes it. The one-to-one programme runs on asynchronous video review over WhatsApp, with the rep confirming 'there's no actual like live sessions after the onboarding' beyond occasional ad hoc calls, and the community tier has no booking option at all: asked directly, the rep answered 'No, not really.' This is the single reason the deal was lost.

unmet_demand.want: An unbundled option — form coaching and programming without the nutrition and daily accountability components
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Explicitly refused as a matter of policy. The rep stated 'the only, like, actual one-on-one option is just everything we've just gone over. Like, we don't take things out of it. It's just everything one-on-one or not, because he does want to make sure that he can control the outcome.' A capable, self-directed buyer who wants only one of the three pillars has nothing to buy between $200 a month and $6,000.

unmet_demand.want: Clear package and pricing options stated upfront
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Asked six times over fifteen minutes and deflected each time so the presentation could run to completion; the final request was answered with a commitment check rather than a number. The information existed and was simply withheld until the end of the script.

unmet_demand.want: Programming for functional scoliosis and hypermobility — building stability and midline strength rather than unlocking stiffness
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The mobility pillar as delivered is built for the opposite presentation. The rep acknowledged his mobility was already good and gestured at stability, but nothing in the offer is designed around a hypermobile dancer with weak adductors, a posterior pelvic tilt difficulty and a scoliosis to balance. Whether the programme can serve this body is untested.
